title: Choose values by coordinates.
lead: One tensor. Five rows and five columns.
captions: Chapter Three keeps the floating-point values on the GPU and arranges them in a five by five tensor. Row and column numbers start at zero.
The first coordinate selects a row; the second selects a column. These logical coordinates identify inputs. PyTorch chooses execution details for the CUDA operation.

title: A row fixes the first coordinate.
lead: The colon includes every column in that row.
captions: Read x, zero, colon. Row zero is fixed, while the colon includes all columns. Trace the five highlighted inputs from left to right.
Selecting the row chooses the inputs. Multiplying each selected value by two is a separate calculation, which we will inspect next.

title: Multiply the selected row.
lead: Each selected value has one corresponding result.
captions: Each output is twice its selected input. The source coordinates beside the values show where every input came from in the original tensor.
This multiplication creates a new result tensor. It leaves the original x unchanged. Selecting a row and calculating its outputs are different parts of the expression.

title: A column fixes the second coordinate.
lead: The colon now includes every row.
captions: Now read x, colon, zero. The column is fixed, while the colon includes all rows. We take one input from each row.
The first row and first column share their first value, but the other inputs differ. Both selections still contain five values.

title: Multiply the selected column.
captions: Multiply each column input by two. Each result uses one highlighted input; we are not adding the five values into a single total.
This is elementwise multiplication: apply the operation separately to each selected value. Changing from a row to a column changes the inputs, while the multiplier stays fixed.

title: Change only the index.
lead: Index one means the second row or column.
captions: With index one, a row selection chooses the second row. A column selection chooses the second column. Compare their five inputs in the diagram.
Keep the multiplier fixed and explain which coordinates changed. A different selection can change the values without changing the number of inputs or the calculation applied to each.

title: Pause: interpret this expression.
lead: Predict the selected inputs before multiplying.
captions: Try x, colon, three, then multiply by two. Before checking, identify which dimension is fixed and which dimension the colon includes.
Trace the five input cells, then predict their five outputs. Does index three mean the fourth row or the fourth column here? Pause and explain.

title: The second coordinate fixes the column.
lead: All rows. Column three. Five selected inputs.
captions: Index three fixes the fourth column because counting starts at zero. The colon includes every row. The diagram follows those five inputs into their doubled results.
The original tensor is unchanged. Return to Chapter Three, change only a row or column index, and explain the selected inputs before pressing Run.
